inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted ~231.0m (Q2 2026 XBRL share count 229.86m plus ~1m dilutive options/RSUs). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and Indicor was all-cash (debt-funded), so there is no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow share-based compensation add-back, TTM to Q2 2026 (FY2025 47.8 + H1-26 23.6 - H1-25 22.3). Equity-award withholding taxes not separately tagged; immaterial for AMETEK (SBC ~0.6% of revenue).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~9.5%; post-Indicor debt ~11% of capital at ~4.0% after tax -> WACC ~8.9%, rounded to 8.5% for a diversified, low-cyclicality niche-instrument compounder with 20-year margin record. One WACC across scenarios; risk is carried in the bear flows, not a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, no double count.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: US diversified industrial operating company; no bank/REIT/holdco features). First valuation of AME. BASE PERIOD: TTM to 30 Jun 2026 rather than FY2025 so that H1-2026 cash flow (already reflected in the June balance sheet via debt paydown) is not counted twice. NET DEBT: June 2026 debt 2,036 - cash 495 = 1,541, plus ~5,000 of new borrowing for the all-cash Indicor Instrumentation acquisition (closed 26-Aug-2026) = 6,541 pro forma; cross-check: mgmt's ~2.3x leverage at close on ~2.84bn pro forma EBITDA ~ 6.5bn. Q3 operating cash between July and close ignored (conservative). FY2025 XBRL TotalDebt (3,492) looks inflated relative to adjacent quarters and was not used. REVENUE: year 1 (Jul-26..Jun-27) = TTM x ~1.06 organic + ~10 months of Indicor (~$1.1bn/yr -> ~$0.92bn) = +17.7%; year 2 adds the last 2 months of Indicor plus ~5% organic. Beyond that growth is ORGANIC ONLY: AMETEK's historical 8-10% revenue CAGR is part-acquired with FCF, and owner FCF here is treated as fully distributable, so compounding acquired growth on top would count the reinvested cash twice. EBITDA margin is pre-SBC (XBRL EBITDA = operating income + D&A, which is post-SBC; TTM 31.2% + SBC 0.6% = 31.9%); Indicor assumed ~30% EBITDA margin, diluting the blend slightly in year 1. D&A includes large acquired-intangible amortisation (~5.3% of revenue TTM, higher post-Indicor) and glides to ~capex+ by year 10 so the amortisation tax shield is not perpetuated. Working capital: manufacturer, capture -10% of revenue change (slightly over-charges year 1 because Indicor's working capital was bought with the purchase price). BUYBACKS: AMETEK is a repurchaser (FY2025 $434m, H1-26 $28m) so the flat count is funded, though repurchases will pause while Indicor debt is paid down.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~12.4%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (6.4%): book value is swollen by retained earnings reinvested in acquisitions (goodwill/intangibles), not by organic growth. EPS 3yr CAGR selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 revenue 6,150.5 -> 7,401.1. Revenue 5yr CAGR null: FY2018-FY2021 annual revenue is missing from the XBRL-derived CSV. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2020 1,165, FY2022 963, FY2025 1,624. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (19%) starts from a working-capital-depressed FY2022 and overstates the trend; the 5yr (6.9%) is closer to the underlying rate. SBC grew roughly with revenue, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are near identical.

base.narrative: Indicor integrated on plan, organic growth ~5-6% on record backlog, OpEx lifts blended EBITDA margin ~1pp.

bull.narrative: Aerospace/defense and automation upcycle converts the +28% order book, Indicor margins lifted toward AMETEK's ~33%+ EBITDA level.

bear.narrative: Industrial destocking and tariff drag turn organic growth negative in year 1, Indicor underdelivers, margins give back ~2pp.

scenario_narratives.base: Indicor Instrumentation (~$1.1bn sales, recurring consumables/aftermarket) is folded into EIG and EMG on AMETEK's usual Operational Excellence playbook; the record $4.1bn backlog and +25% organic orders support ~6% organic growth next year fading to ~3-4% as aerospace/defense and process-instrument cycles normalise. Tariff costs (~$70m in 2025) continue to be priced through. Blended EBITDA margin dips on Indicor in year 1 then recovers ~1pp. Free cash flow goes to deleveraging from ~2.3x rather than buybacks or new deals; no further acquisitions are credited.
scenario_narratives.bull: The order surge (+28%, EMG +35% organic) proves to be the front end of a multi-year aerospace, defense and automation upcycle, sustaining 7-9% organic growth for several years; AMETEK lifts Indicor's margins to group level as it has with prior deals, pushing pre-SBC EBITDA margin toward 34%. The market continues to pay a premium multiple for a compounder with this record (20x terminal cap).
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 order spike is pre-tariff pull-forward and aerospace restocking that reverses: organic sales fall ~1% next year and grow only 2-3% after, as China exposure and trade policy weigh on process and analytical instruments. Indicor, AMETEK's largest-ever deal, integrates poorly and dilutes margins; with leverage at ~2.3x the compounding M&A engine stalls. Margins give back ~2pp to ~30% and the market re-rates the name to an industrial multiple (15x cap, 2.5% terminal growth).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because the largest acquisition in company history is two months old and leverage is at a 10-year high; the business itself is diversified with no single customer, market or regulator dependency, so the bear is margin/growth disappointment rather than solvency. Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice this year and the backlog supports it. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs both a sustained order upcycle and Indicor margin expansion.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AMETEK is valued as a mature, high-margin niche-instrument compounder on an owner-FCF basis, using organic growth only: the acquisition half of its historical growth algorithm is not credited, because the FCF that would fund future deals is already counted as distributable. Indicor is included from its closing (revenue and the ~$5bn of debt that paid for it).
key_risks_to_valuation: Indicor integration: ~$5bn, the largest deal in AMETEK's history, closed 26-Aug-2026; its margin and growth are assumed, not yet reported
Pro forma net debt is an estimate (June balance sheet + ~$5bn deal debt); the Q3 10-Q will fix it
Order surge may be pull-forward ahead of tariffs or aerospace restocking
Terminal value is roughly three-quarters of EV; the 18x cap binds in the base case
Excluding future M&A is conservative relative to how the market values AMETEK's capital-deployment record
